title: Ibtida': stopping at the end of an ayah and starting again: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: At-Tariq 9 to 17, Al-Burooj 1 to 11 and stopping signs
source: Written for quran/y5 lesson 38 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Ibtida' rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 38. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Waqf and ibtida'
points: Waqf: stop on a whole word, with a breath
The last letter becomes sakin when we stop
Ibtida': start again in a place that makes sense

head: Not this
This
rows: Stopping in the middle of a word to breathe
Stop only at the end of a word, and restart where the meaning is complete

keywords.def: stopping on a word, with a breath
a small mark above the line that tells us how to stop

questions.q: Read 85:7 to 8, stopping at the end of 85:7 and starting 85:8 correctly.
Pupil PDF: write how to say six ayah endings when stopping. Today's rota group recites Al-Burooj 1 to 8.
Extend: practise an emergency stop in 85:8 after «بِٱللَّهِ» and restart from «أَن يُؤْمِنُوا۟».
Stretch: why do we not restart from «ٱلْعَزِيزِ» alone?
questions.a: It describes Allah in the phrase before; starting there cuts it off from its meaning.

questions.q: When we stop on «شُهُودٌۭ», we say ...
questions.a: A) shuhood. Dammatan at a stop: drop the vowel.

options: stopping in the middle of a word

questions.q: Think again: If you run out of breath in the middle of an ayah, where should you start again?
questions.a: Go back to a place where the meaning starts well, usually the start of the phrase, then carry on.
